Contrastive Embedding — t-SNE Projection

Each point is one 60-candle window, projected from its 128-dim TFT + InfoNCE embedding down to 2D. Clusters correspond to the regimes the downstream Gaussian HMM discovers — tight, well-separated clusters mean the contrastive pretraining learned a market-state representation the HMM can cleanly partition, rather than a diffuse cloud it has to force boundaries onto.

How this was generated — InfoNCE contrastive learning, in plain English

The encoder is trained to answer one question, over and over: “given this market window, which other window came from a nearby, similar moment — and which windows are unrelated?” It is shown a window and a true positive (an augmented view of the same window), alongside many negatives (unrelated windows), and the InfoNCE loss pulls the positive pair's embeddings together while pushing every negative apart. Repeated over millions of windows, the only way to keep satisfying that objective is to encode the underlying market regime — because regime is the latent property that makes two windows genuinely alike. t-SNE then compresses the resulting 128-dim space to 2D purely for visualization; the clustering it reveals was already present in the embedding, not created by t-SNE itself.
